title: Vatican Challenge Part 5: Cardinal Alessandro Farnese to the nuncio Giovanni Poggio, Rome 15 April 1542 (AAV Segr. Stato Spagna 1A ff. 70r-73v, DECODE R92)

documents.shelfmark: AAV Segr. Stato, Spagna 1A/2, ff. 70r-73v (DECODE R92, ASV_i1025_SdS_Spain_IA-2)
documents.route: Rome -> Giovanni Poggio, bishop of Tropea, nuncio in Spain

plaintext.source: Simon Klee, 'The Farnese letter' (https://simonklee.dk/farnese-letter), published 16 Sept 2026, accepted by MysteryTwister; key and edited Italian, some damaged passages marked uncertain

transcription.source: EHum, 9 Jan 2016, for the MysteryTwister challenge (byte-identical to DECODE R92's DOC_R92_D1633_1633.txt); image-verified re-read by the project 2026-09-18 (IA-2_reread.txt, 6489 digit tokens measured)
transcription.notes: Measured with --digits: 6534 tokens counts single digits plus a few digit tokens in the cleartext frame; 'distinct' 41 counts digit+mark variants (7^. etc.), not signs. NOTES' parse5 count is 6553 digits; Klee's corrected transcription has 6562. The re-read changed 151 positions (62 substitutions, 39 insertions, 22 deletions; four dittographies on 071v, struck digits on 072v/073r); 52 '?' remain at the 071v fold and under blots. No written separators between code groups (Lasry, e-mail 16 Sept 2026).

system.summary: Mixed one-/two-digit monoalphabetic substitution (18 letters, u/v one code, no h, 9 = null, 81 = et) with unwritten code boundaries, plus a small layer of dotted pairs for ce/ci/qua/que/qui, non and three titles (Klee's key).

diacritics.note: A dot on one digit of a two-digit code selects a syllable, 'non' or an abbreviated title (27^=ce, 2^7=qua, 7^2=que, 72^=ci, 57^=non, 5^7=qui, 0^5=S.S.ta, 40^=S.M.ta, 6^0=V.S.).

system.doubled_letters: written once (doubled digits strongly suppressed, 0.30 of chance; Farnese chancery rule 'senza duplicare le consonanti', Meister p. 223)
system.sibling_key: Spain IA-1 (DECODE R91, same volume, Dec 1541) is a different key; Meister 1906 keys nos. 1-3 (Montepulciano/Poggio 1539-42, Piacenza 1545) and Lasry's S6 key (1568-70) tested and excluded; none used.
system.notes: Null 9 occurs 365 times in Klee's alignment. The project's own diagnosis (4 = null, vowel digits {7,0,3,1}, Antonio Elio polyphonic-syllabic design) is superseded by Klee's key: 4 = o, 9 = null. distinct_symbols counts the 20 undotted codes plus 9 dotted codes of key.md.

prior_solution.where: Simon Klee, 'The Farnese letter', simonklee.dk, 16 Sept 2026 (submitted to MysteryTwister 15 Sept, accepted). Published while this project's attack (14-18 Sept) was running; the project recorded it only on 20 Sept.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. Target-specific: resumed the target with a directive to solve it (15 Sept), opened a DECODE account and downloaded R91/R92 (16-18 Sept), relayed George Lasry's e-mail that the manuscript has no separators, and brought in and credited Klee's solution (20 Sept commit, no model trailer).
tools: lattice/beam-Viterbi solver with simulated annealing (native/Program5.cs, vsolve.exe)

synthetic matched controls (make_syn.py, syn_tri.py, vc_syn.py, elio_syn.py, synk2.py)

solution.what: Took the MysteryTwister Part 5 transcript (EHum 2016) and the solved Part 4 sibling transcript (Portugal IA-1).
Mutual-information diagnostics: digit 4 behaves as a null/word separator, 8 and 5 never end words, dotted digits mostly 7/2/0. The null diagnosis was wrong (Klee: 4 = o, 9 = null).
C# lattice solver (polyphonic singles, dotted singles, 2- and 3-digit codes; 5-gram LM + KL + MDL + word coverage) on the real text: no convergent key.
Synthetic key-1-style cipher: the pure LM objective is not identifiable; dictionary coverage separates true from wrong keys.
Meister 1906 keys nos. 1-3 (Montepulciano, the Poggio key 'mandata per il Montepulciano', Piacenza 1545) applied under trigram likelihood: all score below search optima.
Exact bi/trigram partition likelihood, annealing 21 letters over 9 digits (polyphonic single-digit model), Italian: 24 runs, 24 different keys, chance-level agreement.
Same search on a 7000-letter synthetic polyphonic cipher (syn_tri.py) recovers the true key.
Plaintext Spanish: 12 runs under a Don Quijote trigram model, no convergence.
Two-digit syllables on a fixed phase (vowel slots {2,0,7,5} after the Meister key-1 dot rule): no even/odd difference.
Word-final enrichment and frequency mass put the vowel-bearing digits at {7,0,3,1}. Wrong under Klee's key (7=n, 0=s, 3=m, 1=u/v).
Partition search constrained to vowels {7,0,3,1} (vc.py): 24 runs, agreement 0.861 against chance 0.799.
Matched synthetic with the believed structure (vc_syn.py): key recovered at 0.97 and 0.93 on two seeds, so the real text was judged not a polyphonic single-digit substitution.
Lattice solver with --null=4 --vowdig=7031 --consdig=85269: Italian-looking decodes but no convergence across four seeds; the word-coverage metric shown to be gameable.

One key across all pages (chi-squared), doubled digits suppressed, 27 and 80 as dominant word-final units, 441 repeated 7-grams, BPE units mostly one to three digits: diagnosed a variable-length syllabic code with nomenclature. The one-key and one/two-digit-unit findings fit Klee's key; the syllabic/nomenclature reading did not.
Lasry-Megyesi-Kopal 2021 and Lasry-Simonetta-Biermann HistoCrypt 2025 read; the cipher was identified as an Antonio Elio polyphonic-syllabic design. This identification was wrong.
Global two-digit grid tested in three phasings (gphase.py): none exists; units are variable-length.
DECODE R92 image route probed without a login: only 200x256 thumbnails, unreadable.
Elio-design synthetic (elio_syn.py) does not reproduce the real text's consonant runs or repetition; read as evidence of a nomenclature layer.

Clear copies located (BAV Chigi L III 65 ff. ~165-190, AAV Lettere de' Principi 14 A, Naples Carte Farnesiane 723) and key volume Chigi M II 49; none digitised. Meister pp. 176-178, 222-224 re-read from scans.

EM segmentation into one- and two-digit units (41 types, incl. 80, 57, 27, 03, 73) then unit-level annealing (usolve.py): fails on real text and on its synthetic control; oracle shows a pre-fixed segmentation caps the score.
DECODE account obtained (human); George Lasry confirms by e-mail that the Part 5 manuscript has no visual separators between tokens.

Downloaded R92 (eight 400-dpi images, transcription, address leaf) and R91 (IA-1 sibling). R92 transcription byte-identical to the challenge text; no interlinear decipherment (faint writing is show-through).
Seven page agents re-read every cipher line of 070r-073r against the images (IA-2_reread.txt): 151 positions corrected, dots checked. Structural statistics unchanged.
Spain IA-1 (R91): different digit profile and no doubling suppression, so a different key.
Doubled-digit rate as a relabelling invariant: no renumbering of Meister keys 1 or 2, nor any single-digit polyphonic design, gives IA-2's rate.
DECODE searched for further Farnese/Poggio material; Camera Apostolica R23, R202-R204 fetched: Avignon keys of c. 1379, irrelevant.

Simon Klee's independent solution (published 16 Sept 2026, MysteryTwister-accepted) reviewed and accepted: split-half recoveries agree, synthetic and shuffled controls, manuscript checks, historical corroboration. Key recorded in key.md; the project's own diagnosis marked superseded.

outcome.fraction_read_source: No reading file in vatican5/: the project's attacks gave no cipher token a value. Klee's published alignment (outside this project) accounts for 6358 of 6562 corrected digit tokens exactly, 170 by recorded departures, 34 in gaps.
outcome.notes: Not read by this project after seven sessions; it misdiagnosed the system as an Antonio Elio polyphonic-syllabic cipher with 4 as null. Solved independently by Simon Klee (key in key.md, credit his). key = none refers to this project's recovery; Klee's key is complete. Verification lists Klee's checks as reviewed here on 20 Sept 2026 (SOLUTION.md).
